name: Records That Rewired the Radio: Blues to Streaming
description: The songs, albums and sounds, from the blues and jazz of the early 1900s to reggae, hip-hop, K-pop and streaming, that sent popular music in new directions.

checkpoints.name: Roots
checkpoints.note: African American communities in the South create the blues and then jazz, and a few singers turn music into a statement of protest.

checkpoints.name: Rock and roll
checkpoints.note: Electric guitars, young listeners and radio create a teenage music, led by Elvis Presley, while jazz and Brazil explore calmer, subtler sounds.

checkpoints.name: The album age
checkpoints.note: Bands treat a whole record as one work, using the studio as an instrument. Bob Dylan's songs bring a new kind of lyric to the charts, reggae and Bob Marley carry Jamaican music abroad, and music takes on war, race and politics.

checkpoints.name: Punk, rap and video
checkpoints.note: Punk tears up the rules, rap moves from the Bronx to the charts, and music videos make a pop star global.

checkpoints.name: Global pop
checkpoints.note: Grunge, hip-hop, Cuban and Korean music and online video break the barriers between countries and between charts, and from 2008 streaming services such as Spotify change how people hear it all.
